queries.title: Dataset profile
queries.technique: Aggregation
queries.question: How many users are in the experiment and what are the headline rates?
queries.sql:
-- title: Dataset profile
-- technique: Aggregation
-- question: How many users are in the experiment and what are the headline rates?
SELECT
    count(*)                                   AS n_users,
    sum(treatment)::BIGINT                     AS n_treatment,
    (count(*) - sum(treatment))::BIGINT        AS n_control,
    round(avg(treatment), 6)                   AS treatment_share,
    round(avg(visit), 6)                       AS visit_rate,
    round(avg(conversion), 6)                  AS conversion_rate,
    round(avg(exposure), 6)                    AS exposure_rate,
    min(row_id)                                AS min_row_id,
    max(row_id)                                AS max_row_id
FROM experiment;

queries.title: Data quality rule checks
queries.technique: Data quality validation (UNION ALL of rule checks, conditional aggregation)
queries.question: Do the rows satisfy the domain and logical constraints the analysis relies on?
queries.sql:
-- title: Data quality rule checks
-- technique: Data quality validation (UNION ALL of rule checks, conditional aggregation)
-- question: Do the rows satisfy the domain and logical constraints the analysis relies on?
WITH facts AS (
    SELECT
        count(*)                                                        AS n,
        count(*) - count(COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (split)))                    AS dummy_never_used,
        sum((treatment NOT IN (0, 1))::INT)                             AS bad_treatment,
        sum((visit NOT IN (0, 1))::INT)                                 AS bad_visit,
        sum((conversion NOT IN (0, 1))::INT)                            AS bad_conversion,
        sum((exposure NOT IN (0, 1))::INT)                              AS bad_exposure,
        sum((conversion = 1 AND visit = 0)::INT)                        AS conversion_without_visit,
        sum((exposure = 1 AND treatment = 0)::INT)                      AS exposed_in_control,
        count(*) - count(DISTINCT row_id)                               AS duplicate_row_ids,
        sum((isnan(f0) OR isinf(f0) OR isnan(f1) OR isinf(f1) OR isnan(f2) OR isinf(f2)
          OR isnan(f3) OR isinf(f3) OR isnan(f4) OR isinf(f4) OR isnan(f5) OR isinf(f5)
          OR isnan(f6) OR isinf(f6) OR isnan(f7) OR isinf(f7) OR isnan(f8) OR isinf(f8)
          OR isnan(f9) OR isinf(f9) OR isnan(f10) OR isinf(f10) OR isnan(f11) OR isinf(f11))::INT)
                                                                        AS non_finite_feature_rows,
        sum((f0 IS NULL OR f1 IS NULL OR f2 IS NULL OR f3 IS NULL OR f4 IS NULL OR f5 IS NULL
          OR f6 IS NULL OR f7 IS NULL OR f8 IS NULL OR f9 IS NULL OR f10 IS NULL OR f11 IS NULL
          OR treatment IS NULL OR visit IS NULL OR conversion IS NULL OR exposure IS NULL)::INT)
                                                                        AS rows_with_any_null
    FROM experiment
)
SELECT 'no_null_values' AS check_name, 'error' AS severity, rows_with_any_null AS violating_rows, rows_with_any_null = 0 AS passed FROM facts
UNION ALL SELECT 'features_are_finite',            'error', non_finite_feature_rows,   non_finite_feature_rows = 0   FROM facts
UNION ALL SELECT 'treatment_is_binary',            'error', bad_treatment,             bad_treatment = 0             FROM facts
UNION ALL SELECT 'visit_is_binary',                'error', bad_visit,                 bad_visit = 0                 FROM facts
UNION ALL SELECT 'conversion_is_binary',           'error', bad_conversion,            bad_conversion = 0            FROM facts
UNION ALL SELECT 'exposure_is_binary',             'error', bad_exposure,              bad_exposure = 0              FROM facts
UNION ALL SELECT 'row_id_is_unique',               'error', duplicate_row_ids,         duplicate_row_ids = 0         FROM facts
UNION ALL SELECT 'conversion_implies_visit',       'warn',  conversion_without_visit,  conversion_without_visit = 0  FROM facts
UNION ALL SELECT 'control_is_never_exposed',       'warn',  exposed_in_control,        exposed_in_control = 0        FROM facts;

queries.title: Exact duplicate rows
queries.technique: CTE + GROUP BY on all columns, distribution of group sizes
queries.question: How many rows are exact duplicates? (There is no user id, so duplicates cannot be attributed to the same user and are reported, not removed.)
queries.sql:
-- title: Exact duplicate rows
-- technique: CTE + GROUP BY on all columns, distribution of group sizes
-- question: How many rows are exact duplicates? (There is no user id, so duplicates cannot be attributed to the same user and are reported, not removed.)
WITH groups AS (
    SELECT count(*) AS copies
    FROM experiment
    GROUP BY f0, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6, f7, f8, f9, f10, f11, treatment, conversion, visit, exposure
),
by_size AS (
    SELECT
        CASE WHEN copies >= 5 THEN '5+' ELSE copies::VARCHAR END AS copies_per_distinct_row,
        count(*)                AS distinct_rows,
        sum(copies)::BIGINT     AS total_rows
    FROM groups
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    copies_per_distinct_row,
    distinct_rows,
    total_rows,
    round(100.0 * total_rows / sum(total_rows) OVER (), 3) AS pct_of_all_rows
FROM by_size
ORDER BY copies_per_distinct_row;

queries.title: Sample ratio mismatch (SRM)
queries.technique: CTE, chi-square goodness-of-fit computed in SQL
queries.question: Does the observed treatment/control split match the documented 85/15 design?
queries.sql:
-- title: Sample ratio mismatch (SRM)
-- technique: CTE, chi-square goodness-of-fit computed in SQL
-- question: Does the observed treatment/control split match the documented 85/15 design?
WITH design AS (
    SELECT 1 AS treatment, 0.85 AS expected_share
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 0, 1 - 0.85
),
observed AS (
    SELECT treatment, n_users, sum(n_users) OVER () AS n_total FROM v_arm_summary
),
cells AS (
    SELECT
        o.treatment,
        o.n_users                                   AS observed,
        d.expected_share * o.n_total                AS expected,
        o.n_users::DOUBLE / o.n_total               AS observed_share,
        d.expected_share
    FROM observed o JOIN design d USING (treatment)
)
SELECT
    treatment,
    observed,
    round(expected, 1)                                              AS expected,
    round(observed_share, 6)                                        AS observed_share,
    expected_share,
    round(observed - expected, 1)                                   AS excess_users,
    round(sum(power(observed - expected, 2) / expected) OVER (), 4) AS chi_square_1df,
    -- 3.841 is the 5 % critical value for 1 degree of freedom; the exact p-value is computed in SciPy.
    sum(power(observed - expected, 2) / expected) OVER () > 3.841   AS exceeds_5pct_critical_value
FROM cells
ORDER BY treatment DESC;

queries.title: Average treatment effect (intent-to-treat)
queries.technique: CTE pipeline, conditional aggregation, two-proportion z statistic and Wald interval in SQL
queries.question: What is the absolute and relative effect of treatment assignment on visits and conversions?
queries.sql:
-- title: Average treatment effect (intent-to-treat)
-- technique: CTE pipeline, conditional aggregation, two-proportion z statistic and Wald interval in SQL
-- question: What is the absolute and relative effect of treatment assignment on visits and conversions?
WITH long AS (
    SELECT 'visit' AS outcome, treatment, n_users, visits AS successes FROM v_arm_summary
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'conversion', treatment, n_users, conversions FROM v_arm_summary
),
arms AS (
    SELECT
        outcome,
        max(CASE WHEN treatment = 1 THEN n_users END)::DOUBLE   AS n_t,
        max(CASE WHEN treatment = 0 THEN n_users END)::DOUBLE   AS n_c,
        max(CASE WHEN treatment = 1 THEN successes END)::DOUBLE AS x_t,
        max(CASE WHEN treatment = 0 THEN successes END)::DOUBLE AS x_c
    FROM long
    GROUP BY outcome
),
rates AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        x_t / n_t                   AS p_t,
        x_c / n_c                   AS p_c,
        (x_t + x_c) / (n_t + n_c)   AS p_pool
    FROM arms
),
effects AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        p_t - p_c                                               AS ate,
        sqrt(p_t * (1 - p_t) / n_t + p_c * (1 - p_c) / n_c)     AS se_unpooled,
        sqrt(p_pool * (1 - p_pool) * (1 / n_t + 1 / n_c))       AS se_pooled
    FROM rates
)
SELECT
    outcome,
    round(p_c, 6)                               AS control_rate,
    round(p_t, 6)                               AS treatment_rate,
    round(ate, 6)                               AS absolute_effect,
    round(ate - 1.959964 * se_unpooled, 6)      AS ci95_low,
    round(ate + 1.959964 * se_unpooled, 6)      AS ci95_high,
    round(ate / p_c, 4)                         AS relative_effect,
    round(ate / se_pooled, 2)                   AS z_statistic
FROM effects
ORDER BY outcome DESC;

queries.title: Feature profile
queries.technique: Aggregation over the pre-aggregated value table, FIRST_VALUE window, FILTER clause
queries.question: What do the 12 anonymised features look like (cardinality, range, concentration)?
queries.sql:
-- title: Feature profile
-- technique: Aggregation over the pre-aggregated value table, FIRST_VALUE window, FILTER clause
-- question: What do the 12 anonymised features look like (cardinality, range, concentration)?
WITH per_value AS (
    SELECT feature, value, sum(n_users) AS n
    FROM feature_value_stats
    GROUP BY feature, value
),
with_mode AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        first_value(value) OVER (PARTITION BY feature ORDER BY n DESC, value) AS mode_value,
        first_value(n)     OVER (PARTITION BY feature ORDER BY n DESC, value) AS mode_n
    FROM per_value
)
SELECT
    feature,
    count(*)                                                AS distinct_values,
    round(min(value), 4)                                    AS min_value,
    round(max(value), 4)                                    AS max_value,
    round(sum(value * n) / sum(n), 4)                       AS mean_value,
    round(sqrt(sum(n * value * value) / sum(n) - power(sum(value * n) / sum(n), 2)), 4) AS std_value,
    round(any_value(mode_value), 4)                         AS modal_value,
    round(any_value(mode_n) / sum(n), 4)                    AS share_at_modal_value,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE n = 1)                           AS singleton_values
FROM with_mode
GROUP BY feature
ORDER BY CAST(substr(feature, 2) AS INTEGER);

queries.title: Covariate balance (standardised mean differences)
queries.technique: Conditional aggregation over a long table, derived statistics
queries.question: Are pre-treatment features distributed the same way in both arms, as randomisation implies?
queries.sql:
-- title: Covariate balance (standardised mean differences)
-- technique: Conditional aggregation over a long table, derived statistics
-- question: Are pre-treatment features distributed the same way in both arms, as randomisation implies?
WITH moments AS (
    SELECT
        feature,
        treatment,
        sum(n_users)                                AS n,
        sum(value * n_users) / sum(n_users)         AS mean_value,
        sum(value * value * n_users) / sum(n_users) AS mean_sq
    FROM feature_value_stats
    GROUP BY feature, treatment
),
wide AS (
    SELECT
        feature,
        max(CASE WHEN treatment = 1 THEN mean_value END)                         AS mean_t,
        max(CASE WHEN treatment = 0 THEN mean_value END)                         AS mean_c,
        max(CASE WHEN treatment = 1 THEN (mean_sq - mean_value * mean_value) * n / (n - 1) END) AS var_t,
        max(CASE WHEN treatment = 0 THEN (mean_sq - mean_value * mean_value) * n / (n - 1) END) AS var_c
    FROM moments
    GROUP BY feature
)
SELECT
    feature,
    round(mean_c, 5)                                            AS mean_control,
    round(mean_t, 5)                                            AS mean_treatment,
    round((mean_t - mean_c) / sqrt((var_t + var_c) / 2), 5)     AS std_mean_diff,
    round(var_t / var_c, 4)                                     AS variance_ratio,
    abs((mean_t - mean_c) / sqrt((var_t + var_c) / 2)) < 0.1    AS within_0_1_threshold
FROM wide
ORDER BY abs((mean_t - mean_c) / sqrt((var_t + var_c) / 2)) DESC;

queries.title: Segment-level treatment effects
queries.technique: Self-join of arm statistics, per-segment standard errors, cohort comparison
queries.question: How does the visit effect differ across feature segments?
queries.sql:
-- title: Segment-level treatment effects
-- technique: Self-join of arm statistics, per-segment standard errors, cohort comparison
-- question: How does the visit effect differ across feature segments?
WITH arms AS (
    SELECT
        t.feature, t.segment_id, t.segment,
        least(t.value_min, c.value_min)     AS value_min,
        greatest(t.value_max, c.value_max)  AS value_max,
        t.n_users::DOUBLE AS n_t, c.n_users::DOUBLE AS n_c,
        t.visits / t.n_users::DOUBLE        AS p_t,
        c.visits / c.n_users::DOUBLE        AS p_c
    FROM v_segment_arm_stats t
    JOIN v_segment_arm_stats c
      ON t.feature = c.feature AND t.segment_id = c.segment_id
     AND t.treatment = 1 AND c.treatment = 0
)
SELECT
    feature,
    segment,
    round(value_min, 3)                                         AS value_min,
    round(value_max, 3)                                         AS value_max,
    (n_t + n_c)::BIGINT                                         AS n_users,
    round(p_c, 5)                                               AS control_visit_rate,
    round(p_t, 5)                                               AS treatment_visit_rate,
    round(p_t - p_c, 5)                                         AS absolute_effect,
    round(sqrt(p_t * (1 - p_t) / n_t + p_c * (1 - p_c) / n_c), 5) AS std_error,
    round((p_t - p_c) / nullif(p_c, 0), 3)                      AS relative_effect
FROM arms
ORDER BY CAST(substr(feature, 2) AS INTEGER), segment_id;

queries.title: Assignment -> exposure -> visit -> conversion funnel
queries.technique: UNION ALL funnel stages, LAG window for step-to-step rates
queries.question: How far do users in each arm progress, and where does the treatment arm differ?
queries.sql:
-- title: Assignment -> exposure -> visit -> conversion funnel
-- technique: UNION ALL funnel stages, LAG window for step-to-step rates
-- question: How far do users in each arm progress, and where does the treatment arm differ?
WITH stages AS (
    SELECT arm, 1 AS step, 'assigned'  AS stage, n_users     AS users FROM v_arm_summary
    UNION ALL SELECT arm, 2, 'exposed',   exposures   FROM v_arm_summary
    UNION ALL SELECT arm, 3, 'visited',   visits      FROM v_arm_summary
    UNION ALL SELECT arm, 4, 'converted', conversions FROM v_arm_summary
)
SELECT
    arm,
    step,
    stage,
    users,
    round(users::DOUBLE / first_value(users) OVER w, 6)                      AS share_of_assigned,
    -- 'exposed' is not a prerequisite for 'visited', so the step rate is only shown for visit -> conversion.
    CASE WHEN stage = 'converted'
         THEN round(users::DOUBLE / lag(users) OVER w, 6) END                AS conversion_given_visit
FROM stages
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY arm ORDER BY step)
ORDER BY arm DESC, step;

queries.title: Exposure non-compliance and the Wald (IV) estimator
queries.technique: Scalar subqueries / CROSS JOIN of arm rows, ratio estimator
queries.question: Only a few treated users are actually exposed. What effect per exposed user does the intent-to-treat effect imply, under the exclusion restriction?
queries.sql:
-- title: Exposure non-compliance and the Wald (IV) estimator
-- technique: Scalar subqueries / CROSS JOIN of arm rows, ratio estimator
-- question: Only a few treated users are actually exposed. What effect per exposed user does the intent-to-treat effect imply, under the exclusion restriction?
WITH t AS (SELECT * FROM v_arm_summary WHERE treatment = 1),
     c AS (SELECT * FROM v_arm_summary WHERE treatment = 0)
SELECT
    round(t.exposure_rate, 6)                                               AS exposure_rate_treatment,
    round(c.exposure_rate, 6)                                               AS exposure_rate_control,
    round(t.visit_rate - c.visit_rate, 6)                                   AS itt_visit,
    round(t.conversion_rate - c.conversion_rate, 6)                         AS itt_conversion,
    round((t.visit_rate - c.visit_rate) / (t.exposure_rate - c.exposure_rate), 4)           AS effect_per_exposed_user_visit,
    round((t.conversion_rate - c.conversion_rate) / (t.exposure_rate - c.exposure_rate), 4) AS effect_per_exposed_user_conversion
FROM t CROSS JOIN c;

queries.title: File-order structure (why splits must be hash-based)
queries.technique: NTILE window to form position cohorts, LAG for block-over-block change
queries.question: The data has no timestamp or test id. Is row order random, or would a sequential sample / head-tail split be biased?
queries.sql:
-- title: File-order structure (why splits must be hash-based)
-- technique: NTILE window to form position cohorts, LAG for block-over-block change
-- question: The data has no timestamp or test id. Is row order random, or would a sequential sample / head-tail split be biased?
WITH blocks AS (
    SELECT ntile(20) OVER (ORDER BY row_id) AS block, row_id, treatment, visit, f0 FROM experiment
),
agg AS (
    SELECT
        block,
        min(row_id)         AS first_row_id,
        count(*)            AS n_users,
        avg(treatment)      AS treatment_share,
        avg(visit)          AS visit_rate,
        avg(f0)             AS mean_f0
    FROM blocks
    GROUP BY block
)
SELECT
    block,
    first_row_id,
    n_users,
    round(treatment_share, 4)                                               AS treatment_share,
    round(treatment_share - lag(treatment_share) OVER (ORDER BY block), 4)  AS share_change_vs_prev_block,
    round(visit_rate, 5)                                                    AS visit_rate,
    round(visit_rate / avg(visit_rate) OVER (), 2)                          AS visit_rate_vs_block_mean,
    round(mean_f0, 3)                                                       AS mean_f0
FROM agg
ORDER BY block;

queries.title: Train / validation / test split integrity
queries.technique: GROUP BY with window share, uniqueness check against leakage
queries.question: Are the modelling splits disjoint, correctly sized, and comparable?
queries.sql:
-- title: Train / validation / test split integrity
-- technique: GROUP BY with window share, uniqueness check against leakage
-- question: Are the modelling splits disjoint, correctly sized, and comparable?
SELECT
    split,
    count(*)                                            AS n_users,
    round(count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 4)          AS share_of_rows,
    count(*) - count(DISTINCT row_id)                   AS duplicate_row_ids,
    round(avg(treatment), 5)                            AS treatment_share,
    round(avg(visit), 5)                                AS visit_rate,
    round(avg(conversion), 5)                           AS conversion_rate,
    min(split_bucket)                                   AS min_bucket,
    max(split_bucket)                                   AS max_bucket
FROM experiment
GROUP BY split
ORDER BY min_bucket;

queries.title: Stratified vs pooled effect (Simpson's paradox check)
queries.technique: Multi-CTE post-stratification, weighted average of within-stratum effects
queries.question: Does the pooled effect agree with a size-weighted average of within-segment effects for every feature?
queries.sql:
-- title: Stratified vs pooled effect (Simpson's paradox check)
-- technique: Multi-CTE post-stratification, weighted average of within-stratum effects
-- question: Does the pooled effect agree with a size-weighted average of within-segment effects for every feature?
WITH strata AS (
    SELECT
        feature, segment_id,
        sum(n_users)                                                            AS n,
        sum(visits) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1)::DOUBLE
            / sum(n_users) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1)                         AS p_t,
        sum(visits) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0)::DOUBLE
            / sum(n_users) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0)                         AS p_c
    FROM v_segment_arm_stats
    GROUP BY feature, segment_id
),
stratified AS (
    SELECT
        feature,
        sum(n * (p_t - p_c)) / sum(n)   AS stratified_effect,
        min(p_t - p_c)                  AS min_stratum_effect,
        max(p_t - p_c)                  AS max_stratum_effect
    FROM strata
    GROUP BY feature
),
pooled AS (
    SELECT max(visit_rate) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1)
         - max(visit_rate) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0) AS pooled_effect
    FROM v_arm_summary
)
SELECT
    s.feature,
    round(p.pooled_effect, 6)                           AS pooled_effect,
    round(s.stratified_effect, 6)                       AS stratified_effect,
    round(s.stratified_effect - p.pooled_effect, 6)     AS difference,
    round(s.min_stratum_effect, 6)                      AS min_stratum_effect,
    round(s.max_stratum_effect, 6)                      AS max_stratum_effect,
    s.min_stratum_effect > 0                            AS all_strata_positive
FROM stratified s CROSS JOIN pooled p
ORDER BY CAST(substr(s.feature, 2) AS INTEGER);

queries.title: Highest- and lowest-response segments
queries.technique: RANK() window with QUALIFY, minimum-sample guard
queries.question: Which segments show the largest and smallest visit effect, among segments with enough control users to estimate it?
queries.sql:
-- title: Highest- and lowest-response segments
-- technique: RANK() window with QUALIFY, minimum-sample guard
-- question: Which segments show the largest and smallest visit effect, among segments with enough control users to estimate it?
WITH effects AS (
    SELECT
        feature,
        segment,
        sum(n_users)::BIGINT                                                    AS n_users,
        sum(n_users) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0)::BIGINT                       AS n_control,
        sum(visits) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1)::DOUBLE
            / sum(n_users) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1)
      - sum(visits) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0)::DOUBLE
            / sum(n_users) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0)                         AS visit_effect
    FROM v_segment_arm_stats
    GROUP BY feature, segment
    HAVING sum(n_users) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0) >= 1000
)
SELECT
    feature,
    segment,
    n_users,
    n_control,
    round(visit_effect, 5)                              AS visit_effect,
    rank() OVER (ORDER BY visit_effect DESC)            AS rank_highest,
    rank() OVER (ORDER BY visit_effect ASC)             AS rank_lowest
FROM effects
QUALIFY rank_highest <= 5 OR rank_lowest <= 5
ORDER BY visit_effect DESC;

queries.title: Two-way interaction grid with subtotals
queries.technique: GROUPING SETS with GROUPING() to label subtotal rows
queries.question: Do two engagement-like features (f0 and f8 off their modal value) interact in the treatment effect?
queries.sql:
-- title: Two-way interaction grid with subtotals
-- technique: GROUPING SETS with GROUPING() to label subtotal rows
-- question: Do two engagement-like features (f0 and f8 off their modal value) interact in the treatment effect?
WITH modes AS (
    SELECT feature, value AS mode_value FROM v_feature_segments WHERE segment_id = 0
),
flags AS (
    SELECT
        e.treatment,
        e.visit,
        e.f0 <> (SELECT mode_value FROM modes WHERE feature = 'f0') AS f0_non_modal,
        e.f8 <> (SELECT mode_value FROM modes WHERE feature = 'f8') AS f8_non_modal
    FROM experiment e
)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN grouping(f0_non_modal) = 1 THEN 'ALL' ELSE f0_non_modal::VARCHAR END AS f0_non_modal,
    CASE WHEN grouping(f8_non_modal) = 1 THEN 'ALL' ELSE f8_non_modal::VARCHAR END AS f8_non_modal,
    count(*)                                                    AS n_users,
    round(avg(visit) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0), 5)           AS control_visit_rate,
    round(avg(visit) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1), 5)           AS treatment_visit_rate,
    round(avg(visit) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1)
        - avg(visit) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0), 5)           AS visit_effect
FROM flags
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((f0_non_modal, f8_non_modal), (f0_non_modal), (f8_non_modal), ())
ORDER BY grouping(f0_non_modal), grouping(f8_non_modal), f0_non_modal, f8_non_modal;

queries.title: Feature quantiles by arm
queries.technique: Ordered-set aggregates (quantile_cont) with PIVOT
queries.question: Beyond means, do the feature distributions line up between arms at the median and tails?
queries.sql:
-- title: Feature quantiles by arm
-- technique: Ordered-set aggregates (quantile_cont) with PIVOT
-- question: Beyond means, do the feature distributions line up between arms at the median and tails?
WITH q AS (
    SELECT
        feature,
        CASE WHEN treatment = 1 THEN 'treatment' ELSE 'control' END AS arm,
        quantile_cont(value, 0.50) AS p50,
        quantile_cont(value, 0.90) AS p90,
        quantile_cont(value, 0.99) AS p99
    FROM v_feature_long
    GROUP BY feature, treatment
)
SELECT *
FROM (PIVOT q ON arm USING first(round(p50, 4)) AS p50, first(round(p90, 4)) AS p90, first(round(p99, 4)) AS p99 GROUP BY feature)
ORDER BY CAST(substr(feature, 2) AS INTEGER);

queries.title: Visit x conversion co-occurrence by arm
queries.technique: Contingency table with windowed shares (SUM() OVER PARTITION BY)
queries.question: How do the two outcomes relate, and is conversion-given-visit different between arms? (Conditioning on visit is post-treatment: descriptive only.)
queries.sql:
-- title: Visit x conversion co-occurrence by arm
-- technique: Contingency table with windowed shares (SUM() OVER PARTITION BY)
-- question: How do the two outcomes relate, and is conversion-given-visit different between arms? (Conditioning on visit is post-treatment: descriptive only.)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN treatment = 1 THEN 'treatment' ELSE 'control' END    AS arm,
    visit,
    conversion,
    count(*)                                                       AS n_users,
    round(count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY treatment), 6)         AS share_of_arm,
    round(count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY treatment, visit), 6)  AS share_within_visit_group
FROM experiment
GROUP BY treatment, visit, conversion
ORDER BY arm DESC, visit, conversion;

queries.title: Development-sample representativeness
queries.technique: Cohort comparison with a z statistic per metric (UNPIVOT + self-join)
queries.question: Is the ~5 % development sample a fair miniature of the full dataset?
queries.sql:
-- title: Development-sample representativeness
-- technique: Cohort comparison with a z statistic per metric (UNPIVOT + self-join)
-- question: Is the ~5 % development sample a fair miniature of the full dataset?
WITH cohorts AS (
    SELECT
        CASE WHEN sample_bucket < 5 THEN 'dev_sample' ELSE 'rest_of_data' END AS cohort,
        count(*)::DOUBLE    AS n,
        avg(treatment)      AS treatment_share,
        avg(visit)          AS visit_rate,
        avg(conversion)     AS conversion_rate,
        avg(exposure)       AS exposure_rate
    FROM experiment
    GROUP BY 1
),
long AS (
    UNPIVOT cohorts ON treatment_share, visit_rate, conversion_rate, exposure_rate INTO NAME metric VALUE rate
)
SELECT
    s.metric,
    s.n::BIGINT                     AS n_dev_sample,
    r.n::BIGINT                     AS n_rest,
    round(s.rate, 6)                AS dev_sample_rate,
    round(r.rate, 6)                AS rest_rate,
    round((s.rate - r.rate)
        / sqrt(s.rate * (1 - s.rate) / s.n + r.rate * (1 - r.rate) / r.n), 2) AS z_statistic
FROM long s
LEFT JOIN long r ON r.metric = s.metric AND r.cohort = 'rest_of_data'
WHERE s.cohort = 'dev_sample'
ORDER BY s.metric;

queries.title: Qini curve of the champion uplift model, in SQL
queries.technique: NTILE ranking, running totals with SUM() OVER, Qini formula
queries.question: If we target users in descending order of predicted uplift, how many incremental visits accumulate on the held-out test split?
queries.sql:
-- title: Qini curve of the champion uplift model, in SQL
-- requires: predictions
-- technique: NTILE ranking, running totals with SUM() OVER, Qini formula
-- question: If we target users in descending order of predicted uplift, how many incremental visits accumulate on the held-out test split?
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT
        treatment,
        visit,
        ntile(20) OVER (ORDER BY visit__s_learner_gbm DESC, row_id) AS bucket
    FROM predictions
    WHERE split = 'test'
),
per_bucket AS (
    SELECT
        bucket,
        count(*)                                        AS n_users,
        sum(treatment)                                  AS n_t,
        sum(1 - treatment)                              AS n_c,
        sum(visit) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1)         AS y_t,
        sum(visit) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0)         AS y_c
    FROM ranked
    GROUP BY bucket
),
running AS (
    SELECT
        bucket,
        sum(n_users) OVER w AS cum_users,
        sum(n_t) OVER w     AS cum_n_t,
        sum(n_c) OVER w     AS cum_n_c,
        sum(y_t) OVER w     AS cum_y_t,
        sum(y_c) OVER w     AS cum_y_c,
        sum(n_users) OVER () AS total_users,
        sum(n_t) OVER ()    AS total_n_t
    FROM per_bucket
    WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY bucket ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
)
SELECT
    bucket,
    round(cum_users / total_users, 2)                               AS fraction_targeted,
    cum_y_t::BIGINT                                                 AS cum_treated_visits,
    cum_y_c::BIGINT                                                 AS cum_control_visits,
    round(cum_y_t - cum_y_c * cum_n_t / cum_n_c, 1)                 AS qini_incremental_visits,
    round(1000 * (cum_y_t / cum_n_t - cum_y_c / cum_n_c) * cum_users / total_users, 3)
                                                                    AS incremental_visits_per_1000_users,
    round(last_value(cum_y_t - cum_y_c * cum_n_t / cum_n_c) OVER (ORDER BY bucket
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) * cum_users / total_users, 1)
                                                                    AS random_targeting_baseline
FROM running
ORDER BY bucket;

queries.title: Predicted vs observed uplift by decile
queries.technique: NTILE deciles, predicted-vs-actual comparison, standard error per decile
queries.question: Within each decile of predicted uplift, does the observed treatment-minus-control difference match the prediction?
queries.sql:
-- title: Predicted vs observed uplift by decile
-- requires: predictions
-- technique: NTILE deciles, predicted-vs-actual comparison, standard error per decile
-- question: Within each decile of predicted uplift, does the observed treatment-minus-control difference match the prediction?
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT
        treatment,
        visit,
        visit__s_learner_gbm AS predicted_uplift,
        ntile(10) OVER (ORDER BY visit__s_learner_gbm DESC, row_id) AS decile
    FROM predictions
    WHERE split = 'test'
),
agg AS (
    SELECT
        decile,
        count(*)                                            AS n_users,
        avg(predicted_uplift)                               AS mean_predicted_uplift,
        avg(visit) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1)             AS p_t,
        avg(visit) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0)             AS p_c,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 1)::DOUBLE       AS n_t,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE treatment = 0)::DOUBLE       AS n_c
    FROM ranked
    GROUP BY decile
)
SELECT
    decile,
    n_users,
    round(mean_predicted_uplift, 5)                                     AS mean_predicted_uplift,
    round(p_t - p_c, 5)                                                 AS observed_uplift,
    round(sqrt(p_t * (1 - p_t) / n_t + p_c * (1 - p_c) / n_c), 5)       AS std_error,
    round((p_t - p_c) - mean_predicted_uplift, 5)                       AS calibration_gap
FROM agg
ORDER BY decile;
